verdict.rationale:
There is concrete evidence Google responded to a real vulnerability (the 2019 Bluetooth pairing flaw) by offering a replacement program, but the response reached users only via an ad-hoc support chat/RMA process (pay $1.07, wait for email) rather than a documented advisory with affected-model lookup, and firmware itself cannot be updated in-field — flawed keys were physically replaced, not patched. No official docs describe an advisory feed, CVE tracking, or a lookup tool for affected serial/model numbers.
missing for 10: published security advisories/CVE list, an affected-model or serial lookup tool, an official firmware-update mechanism or changelog, first-party confirmation of the replacement process (only community reports exist).
